headline: Approved use of Opioid Settlement funding for a PrideStar EMS buprenorphine program and a Title V septic variance for 31 Pemberton Street.
summary: The board approved the June 3, 2026 minutes, reviewed PrideStar EMS reports, and voted to recommend Opioid Settlement funding for a pre-hospital buprenorphine administration program. The board also approved a Title V variance for an alternative septic system at 31 Pemberton Street. Staff reviewed development services reports, mosquito control updates, and a tobacco permit violation at Lowell Quick Stop Corp, with the owner asked to appear at the September 2, 2026 meeting.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the June 3, 2026 Board of Health meeting.
Recommended using Opioid Settlement funding for PrideStar EMS's pre-hospital buprenorphine administration proposal, with all members present voting yes.
Approved the Title V variance request for 31 Pemberton Street and authorized the Director of Health & Human Services to sign related paperwork, with all members present voting yes.

plain_text:
PRESENT: 
Jo-Ann Keegan, Chairperson 
Erin Gendron, Member 
William Galvin, Member 
Kathleen Cullen-Lutter, Member 
Lisa Golden, Director of Health & Human Services 
 
EXCUSED: Alison Keegan, Member 
  
Chairperson Keegan called the August 5, 2026 meeting of the Board of Health to order at 6:00PM 
 
8/5/2026 - Minutes 
1. NEW BUSINESS 
 
1.I. For Approval: Minutes of the June 3, 2026 meeting of the Board of Health 
Motion: To approve the minutes of the June 3, 2026 meeting of the Board of Health by Kathleen Cullen-Lutter, 
seconded by William Galvin.  All in favor. 
 
1.II. For Review: PrideStar EMS, Inc. Reports and Notifications submitted by Jon Kelley 
Jon Kelley, PrideStar EMS, Inc., reviewed the reports with the Board. Mr. Kelley noted that June had the lowest 
number of overdoses since 2011. Mr. Kelley and Jacqueline Allard, LGH Director of Emergency Services, reviewed an 
actual case regarding the use of the 911 system that involved all emergency response providers (Police, Fire, 
PrideStar EMS, and Lowell General Paramedics) as an example of the use of the 911 system.  Mr. Kelley would like to 
add similar narratives to future reports.   
 
1.III. Discussion and Review: PrideStar EMS Pre-hospital Buprenorphine Administration Proposal 
Mr. Kelley reviewed the proposal with the Board.  Dr. Mollie Quip, Pridestar Medical Director and Dr. Audra 
Williams, Addiction Medicine and the Bridge Clinic, were also present to discuss the proposal which would use 
Opioid Settlement funding.  Administration of Buprenorphine assists with withdrawal symptoms and patients are 
four times more likely to enter treatment.  Dr. Galvin inquired if anyone who receives Narcan would receive 
Buprenorphine.  Dr. Quip reviewed the State protocols in place and the updates that will be in place as of August 17, 
2026, and how that will affect the use of Buprenorphine.  Dr. Williams informed the Board that just after the use of 
Narcan is a perfect opportunity to help direct people to treatment, noting that Buprenorphine is very safe.  Director 
Golden informed the Board that this would be an appropriate use of the OSF and she supports this proposal.   
 
Motion: to support this project and recommend the use of the Opioid Settlement funding made by William Galvin, 
seconded by Kathleen Cullen-Lutter.  All in favor. 
 
Vote: to support this project and recommend the use of the Opioid Settlement funding  
Jo-Ann Keegan - Yes 
Erin Gendron - Yes 
William Galvin - Yes 
Kathleen Cullen-Lutter - Yes 
Alison Keegan - excused
BOHM08052026 
Page 2 
 
 
1.IV. 31 Pemberton Street - Title V variance request 
 
Director Golden reviewed the reason for the request with the Board.  Israel Burl with Burl Engineering addressed the 
Board regarding the reason for the variance request.  Mr. Burl noted that this new system would be an alternative 
septic system that would be better for the location due to the water table levels. 
 
Motion: to support the proposed variances and approve Director of Health & Human Services to sign any necessary 
paperwork made by William Galvin, seconded by Kathleen Cullen-Lutter.  All in favor. 
 
Vote: to support the proposed variances and approve Director of Health & Human Services to sign any necessary 
paperwork. 
Jo-Ann Keegan - Yes 
Erin Gendron - Yes 
William Galvin - Yes 
Kathleen Cullen-Lutter - Yes 
Alison Keegan - excused 
 
1.V. For Review: Monthly Development Services Reports Submitted by Matthew Sheehan 
Sr. Sanitary Code Inspector Matthew Sheehan reviewed the reports with the Board. The schools will have biannual 
inspections during the week of September 14, 2026.  Sr. Inspector Sheehan also spoke about the rodent issues in the 
city and how people putting food out for wildlife also attracts the rodents.   
 
1.VI. Informational: School Based Health Summer Schedule 
The Board accepted and placed on file.   
 
1.VII. Informational: Unwanted Medication Takeback Day - September 19, 2026 
The Board accepted and placed on file. 
 
1.VIII. Communication: Central Mass Mosquito Control Program Monthly Spray Schedule 
Director Golden updated the Board regarding area West Nile Virus and EEE positive mosquitoes in the surrounding 
towns, noting there have been no human cases at this time. There have been no positive mosquitoes yet in Lowell, 
but she expects that will change in the future. 
 
2. OLD BUSINESS 
 
2.I. Informational: LA Times 6.19.26 article written by Karen Garcia 
The Board accepted and placed on file. 
 
3. DEPARTMENTAL/DIVISIONAL REPORTS AND UPDATES 
 
3.I. Departmental and Divisional Reports 
Director Golden reviewed the reports with the Board.  Chairwoman Keegan noted that Lowell Quick Stop Corp 189 
E. Merrimack St was found selling tobacco products without a permit for a second time on July 24, 2026. 
Chairperson Keegan requested that the owner of the establishment appear before the Board at the September 2, 
2026 meeting of the Board of Health.
BOHM08052026 
Page 3 
 
 
4. MOTION TO ADJOURN 
4.I. Motion: To Adjourn the August 5, 2026 meeting of the Lowell Board of Health 
Motion: To adjourn the August 5, 2026 meeting of the Lowell Board of Health at 7:05PM made by William Galvin, 
seconded by Erin Gendron.  All in favor. 
 
 
 
 
 
THE NEXT MEETING OF THE LOWELL BOARD OF HEALTH WILL BE HELD ON 
SEPTEMBER 2, 2026 AT 6:00 PM IN 
THE MAYOR'S RECEPTION ROOM, CITY HALL, 375 MERRIMACK ST 2ND FLOOR
